questions.question: Start at 7 on the number line. Jump up to 12. How many jumps did you make?
questions.explain: Count each jump: 7 to 8, 8 to 9, 9 to 10, 10 to 11, 11 to 12. That is 5 jumps. Do not count 7 itself as a jump.

questions.question: Start at 9 on the number line. Jump up to 15. How many jumps did you make?
questions.explain: Count each jump: 9 to 10, 10 to 11, 11 to 12, 12 to 13, 13 to 14, 14 to 15. That is 6 jumps. Do not count 9 itself as the first jump.

questions.question: Start at 14 on the number line. Go back to 10 (that is 4), then go back 2 more. What is 14 − 6?
questions.explain: Going back to 10 takes 4 steps, then 2 more lands on 8. You do not stop at 10, and you do not just give the number you subtracted.

questions.question: Mia has 13 stickers. She gives 8 to her friend. How many does Mia have left?
questions.explain: Start at 8 and jump up to 13: that is 5 jumps, so 13 − 8 = 5. A common trap is counting 8 as the first jump and getting 6.

questions.question: There are 15 apples in a basket. Sam picks 7. How many apples are left?
questions.explain: Go back from 15 to 10 (that is 5), then back 2 more to land on 8. Do not stop at 10.

questions.question: A bird had 12 eggs in its nest. 5 eggs rolled out. How many eggs are left?
questions.explain: Go back from 12 to 10 (that is 2), then back 3 more to land on 7. Stopping at 10 would give you only 2, not the full answer.

questions.question: A bus had 16 kids on it. 9 got off at the stop. How many kids are still on the bus?
questions.explain: Start at 9 and jump up to 16: that is 7 jumps, so 16 − 9 = 7. Do not count 9 as the first jump, and do not stop at 10.

questions.question: Lena has 15 stickers. She gives 7 to her brother. Then she finds 3 more on the floor. How many does she have now?
questions.explain: First: start at 7, jump up to 15, that is 8. Then 8 + 3 = 11. A trap is stopping at 10 (getting 5) and then 5 + 3 = 8.

questions.question: I started at a number. I went back 3 steps to reach 10. Then I went back 4 more steps. What number did I start at?
questions.explain: If going back 3 steps reaches 10, you started at 10 + 3 = 13. Check: 13 − 3 = 10, then 10 − 4 = 6. Starting at 10 means you did not go back at all.

questions.question: A jar had 16 marbles. Leo took out 8. Then he put back 5. How many marbles are in the jar now?
questions.explain: 16 − 8: start at 8, jump up to 16, that is 8. Then 8 + 5 = 13. A trap is counting 8 as a jump and getting 9, then 9 + 5 = 14.

questions.question: Zoe solves 15 − 7. She says: 'Go back to 10. That is 5. So the answer is 5.' What did Zoe do wrong?
options: She added 5 to 10 to get the answer
She counted 10 as one of her back steps
She stopped at 10 and forgot 2 more steps
She went forward on the line instead of back
questions.explain: Zoe went back to 10 (5 steps) but forgot to go back 2 more to reach 8. The full 15 − 7 means going back all 7 steps, not just to 10.

questions.question: Start at 6 on the number line. Count the jumps up to 14. How many jumps is that?
questions.explain: Jump from 6 up to 10, that is 4 jumps. Then 4 more jumps to 14, so 4 and 4 make 8. Do not count 6 itself as a jump.

questions.question: To find 12 − 5, start at 12 on the number line and go back 2 to land on 10. How many more do you go back?
questions.explain: You must go back 5 in all, and you already went back 2, so 3 more jumps take you to 7. Landing on 10 is only halfway, not the answer.

questions.question: What is 11 − 8? Count up from 8 to 11 on the number line.
questions.explain: Count up 9, 10, 11. That is 3 jumps, so 11 − 8 = 3. Begin counting at 9, because 8 is where you stand, not a jump.

questions.question: Noah had 13 grapes. He ate 6 of them. Go back to 10 first, then go back the rest. How many grapes are left?
questions.explain: Go back 3 to land on 10, then go back 3 more to land on 7. Do not stop at 10, and do not take 6 away again after you reach 10.
